questions.note: Height and head placement land close to the reference in the onion, but the body reads as a generic base mesh in bulky clothes: the upper arms are thick uniform tubes, the lower legs are straight pipes with no calf, and the head is narrow at the crown under a spiky crest, so the man reads stockier in the limbs and smaller-headed than drawn.

The outline follows the reference well in the onion: stance width, elbow flare, carbine diagonal and head turn all register. It loses on the boxy shoulder caps that stick out past the reference's, the straight locked legs and pipe-like trouser columns, and the hair crest that breaks the top of the silhouette.

Every listed item is present and roughly where drawn: gaiter, carrier with three mag pouches, antenna behind the left shoulder, pauldrons, forearm guards, gloves, belt, drop-leg rigs, knee pads, boots. Sizes are off on the forearm guards (fat stacked cylinders) and the right pauldron (a flat plate standing off the arm); the knee pads read oversized and pillowy.

No gross clipping visible, but the stack reads assembled rather than worn: a hard step ring where the upper sleeve ends at the elbow, straps that wrap thighs and arms without compressing the cloth, plates and pad straps standing off what they ride on, little contact shadow under straps and plates, and trousers that cling to the seat like leggings.

The kit is bulky in the wrong places: inflated forearm cuffs and thick sleeves, but a flat, thin-looking carrier slab and clean empty-looking pouches where the reference's carrier is laden and lumpy. The shirt is a smooth neoprene skin with no cloth volume, the trousers baggy pipes; the man reads soft and padded rather than lean and loaded.

The carbine's line matches, but neither hand closes on it: the right hand is a loose fist beside the pistol grip with the index finger laid along the receiver, and the left hand's stiff, separated fingers drape over the top rail like a claw with no thumb wrap. The stock floats in front of the right chest without a clear contact. It reads posed, not held.

defects.what: Right hand does not close on the pistol grip: middle, ring and little fingers curl into a loose fist beside the grip with air inside, the index finger lies straight along the receiver; the hand hovers rather than grips.
defects.fix: Wrap the three lower fingers fully round the grip with the web of the hand high in the grip's tang, palm in contact; index along the lower receiver above the trigger guard.

defects.what: Left hand's fingers lie stiff and evenly spaced over the top of the handguard like a claw, no thumb visible under or beside it, fingertips appear to sit into the rail teeth.
defects.fix: Close the hand round the handguard: thumb along the side or over the top, fingers wrapped under, palm pressing the side, fingertips resting on the surface, not in it.

defects.what: Gloves read as smooth rubber mitts: equal sausage fingers, no knuckle pads, panel seams, palm wrinkles or fabric texture; the reference shows padded M-Pact type gloves.
defects.fix: Model the knuckle and finger armour pads, panel seams, fourchettes and bunching at the knuckles; give the backhand a synthetic textile and the palm a suede-like value.

defects.what: The combat shirt reads as a neoprene wetsuit: seamless smooth sleeves and torso with a slight sheen, no folds, seams, cuffs or cloth weave anywhere on the arms or chest.
defects.fix: Matte woven cloth with seams down the sleeve, gathering at the elbow crook and under straps, fabric texture at native scale.

defects.what: The right pauldron is a flat bent sheet with wobbly, dented surfaces and soft rolled rims, like crumpled cloth rather than a rigid moulded shell; its outer edge stands well off the arm.
defects.fix: A rigid moulded shell: smooth continuous curvature, crisp chamfered edges, consistent thickness, seated on the shoulder with its strap pulling it in.

defects.what: Forearm guards (both arms, right shown) are fat stacked cylinders like rolled cuffs, wider than the forearm and not tapering to the wrist; the reference's guards are contoured plates following the forearm.
defects.fix: Shells that follow the forearm's taper and flattened cross-section, thin-walled, strapped close, segmented where the reference shows segments.

defects.what: Hard stepped ring above the left elbow where the simulated upper sleeve ends over the lower sleeve: a clean lip with a dark gap, like two separate tubes.
defects.fix: One continuous sleeve, folds gathering into the elbow crook rather than a seam-like step.

defects.what: Lower trouser legs are straight smooth pipes with no stacking or blousing over the boot, and the camo is large blurred low-frequency blotches that read as a smudged noise texture, not a printed pattern with dirt.
defects.fix: Cloth stacking and bunching above the boot collar, sharper printed pattern at real scale over a near-black base, dirt concentrated at the hems and knees.

defects.what: The soldier's right boot reads as a low trainer: a smooth swoosh-panelled upper, low collar, few visible laces and a thin sole, unlike the reference's chunky lace-up boots with deep lugs.
defects.fix: Mid-height leather and textile upper with visible eyelets and laces to the collar, toe rand, and a thick lugged sole with a heel step.

defects.what: Skin is saturated orange and waxy with flat shading and a broad uniform sheen; eyebrows are dark painted bars with hard lower edges; the temple silhouette on the viewer's right is a straight vertical cut.
defects.fix: Less saturated, varied skin tone (redder cheeks and nose, cooler jaw under stubble), breakup in the specular, hair-strand brows, a rounded temple.

defects.what: Hair is a crest of spiky cones on a shaved scalp, a mohawk tuft that breaks the head silhouette; the reference has short textured hair with front volume and short but covered sides.
defects.fix: Clumped short strands swept up and to one side at the front, tapering to short coverage over the sides and back.

defects.what: Armour plates (pauldrons, upper-arm and forearm guards) are light grey plastic, far lighter than the reference's dark gunmetal; wear is only painted streaks along the edges.
defects.fix: Darker painted-metal or polymer value near the reference's, wear as chips and scuffs on high points and edges with dirt in recesses.

defects.what: The carrier front and pouches read as clean blockout boxes: flat uniform olive-grey with no fabric weave, binding, wear or dirt, and pouch flaps as flat lids; the reference's carrier is worn tan-olive cordura.
defects.fix: Cordura weave at real scale, bound edges, the reference's tan-olive hue, scuffs and dirt on edges, pouch flaps with thickness and sag.

defects.what: Knee pads are soft pillow shells with a uniform clean surface; the strap and buckle behind the soldier's right knee stand off the leg.
defects.fix: Rigid faceted caps with crisp edges and scuffs, straps pulled tight into the trouser cloth.

defects.what: Thigh straps wrap the leg as perfect flat bands with no compression or wrinkling of the trouser cloth beneath; two wire hooks dangle under the drop-leg pouch.
defects.fix: Straps cinch into the cloth with gathers either side; hooks either tucked or removed.

defects.what: The trousers cling to the buttocks and hamstrings like leggings, showing glute anatomy, inconsistent with the baggy legs below.
defects.fix: Stiff trouser cloth hanging from the seat with ease, folds radiating from the crotch and under the belt.

ranked: [D1] [D2] The hold is not a hold: the right hand is a loose fist beside the pistol grip and the left hand drapes stiff fingers over the rail. Real hands wrap, with the palm pressed to the gun.
[D4] The shirt is a neoprene skin: smooth, seamless, slightly shiny sleeves and torso. Real combat shirts gather at the elbows and under straps and show seams and weave.
[D12] The armour plates are light grey plastic with painted edge streaks; the reference's are dark gunmetal with chipped, dirty wear. The value jump makes the kit read toy-like.
[D5] [D6] Hard armour behaves like cloth: the pauldron is dented and wobbly with rolled rims, and the forearm guards are inflated stacked cylinders instead of thin shells following the forearm.
[D13] The carrier and pouches are clean blockout boxes in flat olive-grey; the reference's are worn tan-olive cordura with lumps, binding and dirt.
[D10] The face is orange and waxy with a uniform sheen and painted-on brows; it reads as a game asset next to the reference's weathered skin.
[D11] The hair is a mohawk-like crest of cones that breaks the top of the silhouette.
[D3] The gloves are smooth rubber mitts with sausage fingers, no knuckle pads or seams.
[D9] The soldier's right boot reads as a low trainer with a swoosh upper and a thin sole; both boots lack the reference's chunky lugs and visible lacing.
[D8] The lower trousers are straight pipes with no stacking over the boots, and the camo is blurred blotch noise rather than a printed pattern with dirt.
[D16] Seen from behind, the trousers cling to the seat like leggings, at odds with the baggy legs below.
Straps sit on every surface without biting into it: no compression, gathers or contact shadow under the arm, thigh and knee straps, so each item looks pasted on rather than worn.
[D7] A hard ring above the left elbow where the simulated upper sleeve stops over the lower sleeve gives away two separate meshes.
Mass reads wrong: inflated arms and cuffs but a thin, flat-faced carrier with empty-looking pouches, where the reference is lean in the body and heavy in the kit.
The legs are straight locked columns with no calf or knee shape showing through the cloth, which stiffens the stance next to the reference's.
[D14] Knee pads are soft pillows with clean surfaces instead of rigid faceted caps, and the strap behind the right knee stands off the leg.
The stock hangs in front of the right chest without clear contact with the arm or the carrier; in a real low ready it rests against the chest or under the arm.
The carbine is uniformly clean matte black with no edge wear, next to a heavily worn reference gun, so it reads as a fresh model rather than a used rifle.
[D15] Two wire hooks dangle under the soldier's right drop-leg pouch, and the thigh straps are perfect flat bands round a cylinder.
